posts.author: Midyin
posts.body:
Ok, so I'm planning to make a game using the Action RPG Plugin, and have A LOT of questions, so i figured i would make a thread about the plugin where those of us using it can talk and ask each other questions.
First one, how do i install this thing?
I've seen a couple youtube videos on how to install DLC and one by ALT+SHIFT+NERD Gaming on the Action RPG Plugin, but none of them were very specific. they kinda talk like the viewer should just already know... I don't. I'm 40 and new to all of this. lol
So do i just drag and drop all the files in the zip into "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\RPG Maker MZ\dlc"?

posts.author: ElvenNeko
posts.body:
Don't own MZ so can't test, but usually plugins require you to put .js file in the  yourgamename\js\plugins folder. Then you go to the Maker, tools\plugin manager, add it there, double click on it to configure, and it's working.
If there is additional files, they usually should have the structure simillar to maker's main directory, like image\something, you have folder image and copy new folder there. Also you can read the help file either on creator's site, or by opening the .js file with any text editor - usually help are on the top, before the plugin code.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
I think that onedrive took over your Documents folder so it is in the pathway now.  I am not a fan of the backup online systems that commandeer your computer.  I'd much rather they acted like an empty hard drive that you move stuff in and out of.
Watch a couple plugin installation videos and pay attention to the folder structures involved.  You will use it over and over again, so it's worth the time.

Hey there! I've been making a game using that plugin for a little over a year. Let me tell you, it is NOT beginner friendly.
The way the plugin works, it uses switches and variables to store important data that it will then use in combat, like the angle of attacks, the XY position of the enemies or the "taking damage" state of battlers. It also uses common events to execute upon something happening, such as when a player uses their shield, or when an enemy takes damage or dies.
If you import the plugin into a new project, EVERY SINGLE variable, switch, common event and plugin setting has to be set up manually by you.
So my advice is, use the sample game that's provided with the plugin as a starting point and edit THAT project, which is already set up, instead of dropping the plugins into a blank project (i am speaking from personal experience)
If you have any other question lemme know! I'm not an expert by any means, but i'll do my best to help!
